<issue>
JoinedStr inference returns Const even with MISSING_VALUE

#### Description

When inferring f-string expressions that contain uninferable values, the JoinedStr node incorrectly returns a Const node containing MISSING_VALUE instead of yielding Uninferable.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import astroid

code = '''
name = "John"
result = f"Hello {name}!"
'''

ast = astroid.parse(code)
node = ast['result']
inferred = list(node.inferred())
print(f"Number of inferred values: {len(inferred)}")
print(f"Inferred type: {type(inferred[0])}")
print(f"Inferred value: {inferred[0].value}")
```

Expected behavior: When f-strings contain uninferable parts, the inference should yield `Uninferable` rather than a `Const` node with `MISSING_VALUE`.

The issue becomes more apparent with f-strings that have format specifiers or other complex expressions that might not be fully inferable at static analysis time.
</issue>
